question: to the Commission Marco Falcone (PPE), Caterina Chinnici (PPE), Salvatore De Meo (PPE), Fulvio Martusciello (PPE), Letizia Moratti (PPE), Giusi Princi (PPE), Flavio Tosi (PPE), Massimiliano Salini (PPE) Subject:

Maritime transport is vital to ensuring the territorial continuity of Sardinia and Sicily and to integrating their production and logistical chains in the European single market. Sectoral operators report that the unilateral introduction by certain shipping companies of summer freight surcharges – which took effect on 1 June 2026 and are as high as 50 % for routes that are not subject to public service obligations – has driven up operating costs. These hikes come at a time when the ETS’ extension to include the maritime sector has resulted in increased costs and burdens for the whole supply chain. The very survival of road haulage companies and of the Sicilian and Sardinian productive sectors is at stake, inasmuch as these surcharges could exacerbate the structural disadvantages specific to island regions, reduce competitiveness and even drive up the price of consumer goods and weaken the purchasing power of citizens. Having regard for the economic, social and territorial cohesion principles enshrined in Articles 174-175 TFEU, we ask the Commission: 1.
What initiatives will it take to increase the transparency, fairness and sustainability of maritime freight rates?
Will it promote measures to manage or mitigate the impact of ETS costs on freight transport with a view to preventing inflation?
Does it agree that it should bolster the mechanisms that safeguard the territorial continuity of island regions, potentially by including a dedicated fund in the EU budget?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (26.8.2026) The Commission recognises the importance to address the challenges impacting the economic sustainability and quality of life of the EU islands. In this context, the EU strategy for islands1 adopted in June 2026 sets out a coordinated approach to support islands and unlock their longterm potential. The Commission is aware of the recent rise in freight rates. Rates for commercial maritime transport services are set by market operators and are not governed by EU legislation. Shipping companies must nonetheless comply with the relevant EU competition rules, including bans on anti-competitive agreements and the abuse of a dominant position. The Emissions Trading System (ETS) review proposes changes that also reduce compliance costs for shipping companies, including administrative simplifications and a dedicated EU mechanism to support shipping companies with ETS allowances for the uptake of sustainable fuels and clean propulsion technologies. The current multiannual financial framework (MFF) allows for support tailored to the specific needs of islands, notably through the European Regional Development Fund, the Cohesion Fund and the Connecting Europe Facility. The Commission proposal for the next MFF fully supports the objectives set out in Article 174 of the Treaty to promote economic, social and territorial cohesion in the EU, including by addressing the needs of areas facing severe natural or demographic handicaps, such as islands. The accompanying national and regional partnership proposal provides Member States with flexibility to address structural challenges while setting out the requirement to allocate resources in a manner that considers, inter alia, the specific needs and constraints of islands and outermost regions.
